## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Duccarita Sutta* ("Bad Conduct", Iti 64) is the fifteenth discourse of the section of threes (Tikanipāta) in the *Itivuttaka*. Framed by the standard opening formula of the collection, the discourse addresses the three kinds of bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct. It culminates in verse teaching that a foolish person who fails to make good karma and accumulates extensive bad deeds is reborn, upon the dissolution of the body, directly into hell (*akatvā kusalaṁ kammaṁ katvānākusalaṁ bahuṁ, kāyassa bhedā duppañño nirayaṁ so 'papajjati*) [Cohen 2006].

 Closely resembling parallels are found across early Buddhist verse corpora, including the *Dhammapada* (Dhp 140), the *Udānavarga* (UV 28, Uv Kg 28, UVS 28), the Gāndhārī *Dharmapada* (G-Dhp 201–223), the Chinese *Dharmapada* translations (T 210, T 212, T 213), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 5.174, AN 6.45).
